threads.body: The merged `request_model`, `server_address`, and `server_port` values are only used for metrics. When the outer embedding omits one and the suppressed inner invocation supplies it, the span still lacks the corresponding start attribute. Include these enriched fields in the finish-time span attributes, as inference already does.

The inner `request_stream` and server values are merged here but `_get_attributes()` does not return them, so an outer fetch with those values unset never receives them on its span. Add these enriched start fields to the finish-time attributes.

threads.body: The new suppressed invocation classes call the base with `start_span=False`, but only suppressed inference overrides `_on_stream_chunk`. The base implementation still records time-to-first-chunk and inter-chunk metrics, so streamed suppressed remote-agent and fetch-response invocations (both are passed to `SyncStreamWrapper`/`AsyncStreamWrapper`) emit the metrics these classes promise to suppress. Retain whether this invocation owns telemetry here and make the base stream-timing path a no-op for suppressed invocations, or override it consistently in every suppressed class.

threads.body: Enrichment can fill `data_source_id`, provider, request model, and server fields from the suppressed retrieval, but none are applied to the span at finish. Thus an outer retrieval created without these optional values silently drops the inner values even though its metrics use some of them. Add all enriched non-content fields to the finish attributes.

threads.body:
`WorkflowInvocation` has the same agent-as-tool problem (`tool("x") -> workflow -> tool("x")`). 

Could we have a rule that we don't suppress unless it's an immediate parent. E.g. 

```
- layer A - sets context for A 
   - layer B - removes context for A, set context for B
      - layer A - fine, sets context for A, removes context for B
         - layer A again - suppressed
           - layer B again - not suppressed
```

This way we have generic approach and never need to update / decide when to suppress what. 

Alternative shortcut: we can limit suppression to client operations for now (inference, embeddings, fetch response, etc), etc since duplicate instrumentation on agent framework level are quite uncommon. Same with tools - if model client make a call, then outer agent framework would not see it at all and won't be able to instrument it too, no need to suppress them (at least for now)
